title: Oath and Garden
premise: Orsen Hartwell, a runaway apprentice hiding her identity as a hedge-witch's last student, guides smugglers through the Thornfell mountains until the old gods—silent for three centuries—begin answering prayers again, and every answered prayer leaves a scar on the land. Hunted by the Crown's witch-finders, who believe she caused the awakening, Orsen discovers the gods are stirring because someone is feeding them blood sacrifices to weaponize them against the kingdom. To stop a war that would consume both mortal realms, she must embrace the magic she fled, expose the true culprit—a revered royal chaplain—and choose between destroying the old gods forever or binding herself to them as their living oath-keeper. She binds herself, saving the realm but surrendering the ordinary life she always wanted.
about_author: Theo Ravensworth is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fantasy. Their work blends folklore, moral ambiguity, and landscapes that feel like characters in their own right.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Guiding a smuggler caravan through Thornfell's hidden roads, Orsen hides her hedge-magic even from her closest companions, using it only to read the mountain's moods. When a prayer whispered at a roadside shrine is suddenly, impossibly answered, the pass itself shifts around them. The chapter ends with the caravan buried in rock and Orsen the sole survivor—terrified that something ancient heard her name.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Descending into the lowland town of Marrowgate, Orsen finds shrines defaced, witch-finders posting warrants, and refugees claiming the old gods spoke to them before their crops blackened. She recognizes the blight pattern from her apprenticeship: godscourge, magic that shouldn't exist anymore. A witch-finder captain, Serah Vane, nearly catches her, forcing Orsen to burn her false papers and flee north with nothing but her secrets.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Following her mentor's old letters to a hidden sanctuary, Orsen instead finds the woman who raised her dying, poisoned by something fed to the gods. With her final breath, the hedge-witch reveals that prayers are being answered through sacrifice—and gives Orsen an oath-stone that will let her hear which god is listening. Grief hardens into resolve; Orsen stops running.

chapters.title: The Chaplain's Sermon
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Orsen and Serah Vane. In the holy city of Caelmere, Royal Chaplain Aldous Renwick preaches unity while secretly collecting god-touched relics. Serah, investigating the same blight, begins doubting her orders when evidence points upward, not outward. Orsen infiltrates the cathedral disguised as a pilgrim and overhears Renwick bargaining with something unseen. Both women now hold pieces of a truth neither can say aloud.

chapters.title: Blood in the Reliquary
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Caught snooping in the reliquary, Orsen is saved when Serah arrives—not to arrest her, but because the warrant against Orsen was forged. An uneasy truce forms between witch and witch-finder as they compare notes: Renwick has been sacrificing prisoners to the war-god Vharkun for years, and the recent awakening means he finally has enough power to move. They escape the city together as Renwick declares Orsen an enemy of the faith.

chapters.title: Roads That Bite
chapters.summary: POV: Serah. Pursued through the mountains by Renwick's zealots, Serah narrates the flight, learning the smuggler's roads from Orsen and unlearning a lifetime of doctrine along the way. A zealot ambush costs them their supplies and nearly Serah's life; Orsen saves her with open hedge-magic for the first time, choosing survival over secrecy. In a cave shrine, the oath-stone flares—the goddess Marenne is watching them, and she is afraid.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Marenne manifests in a drowned grove and reveals the full truth: Renwick isn't controlling Vharkun—he's feeding him, and once sated, Vharkun will drag the other gods into a war to reclaim the mortal world. Only an oath-keeper, a mortal bound willingly to all the gods, can seal or release them. Marenne offers Orsen the choice and warns there is no third path. Orsen refuses to decide yet, buying time but angering a god.

chapters.title: Crown and Covenant
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Racing back to Caelmere, Orsen and Serah try to warn the Crown, but Renwick has framed them as the source of the blight, and the queen orders their arrest on sight. Betrayed by the law Serah served, she publicly breaks with the witch-finders, burning her badge at the city gates—an act that turns half the guard to their side. Renwick accelerates his ritual: the final sacrifice is set for the solstice, three days away.

chapters.title: Solstice of Ash
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Atop the cathedral spire, Renwick offers himself as the ultimate sacrifice to crown Vharkun's return. Orsen fights through the ritual circle while Serah holds the guards; when Orsen reaches the altar, she realizes destroying Vharkun alone would shatter all the gods and the land with them. Choosing the burden over the easy vengeance, she accepts Marenne's oath, binding herself as oath-keeper and severing Renwick's channel mid-prayer. Vharkun, unfed and unbound, collapses back into slumber as the spire burns.

chapters.title: Oath and Garden
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. In the aftermath, the gods sleep but no longer silent—Orsen hears them faintly always, a permanent weight behind her eyes. Cleared by a shaken Crown but unwilling to be its instrument, she declines reward and title. With Serah at her side, she returns to Thornfell and plants a garden over her mentor's grave, where the old shrines bloom again. She keeps the roads, keeps the secret, and keeps the oath.
